races.title: State Senate, District 32
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kelly Seyarto
cands.bio: Republican state senator for District 32 since 2022 and former Assembly member for District 67 (2020–2022). Retired Los Angeles County Fire battalion chief after a 35-year firefighting career. Served on the Murrieta City Council from 1997 to 2006 and again from 2016, including four terms as mayor.

endorsements.text: His campaign site lists endorsements from California Professional Firefighters, Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association, Murrieta Police Officers' Association, National Federation of Independent Business and Southern California Newsgroup.
Ballotpedia lists a 2026 endorsement from the Republican Party of California and a voter-guide recommendation from Reform California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented actions or stated positions from Seyarto on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, donor money, police pay, gun laws, abortion or school choice. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022 or 2026. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties. His sponsored-bill list did not load on the page we read, so we could not review what he authored. Sources conflict on his exact birth date, so we left it out.

local.label: Roots 100: Born in La Puente and raised in Baldwin Park and La Verne, then settled in Murrieta in 1991, where he has lived since.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator since 2022 and Assembly member 2020–2022. Murrieta city councilman from 1997 to 2006 and again from 2016, serving as mayor four times. Retired as a Los Angeles County Fire battalion chief after 35 years. Holds a Master of Public Administration.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service in both chambers plus local elected office and a public administration degree, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. His career before office was in firefighting, not law or policy.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service in both chambers plus local elected office and a public administration degree, which fits the high band for writing law and the budget. His career before office was in firefighting, not law or policy.

roots.summary: Born in La Puente and raised in Baldwin Park and La Verne, then settled in Murrieta in 1991, where he has lived since.

cands.name: Tiffanie Tate
cands.bio: Physician (board-certified OB-GYN who practiced about 20 years), U.S. Navy officer 1997–2004, author and radio co-host. Democrat running for California State Senate District 32. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, San Bernardino Young Democrats and California Young Democrats are listed as endorsing her State Senate campaign.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Tate holding elected office, so there is no legislative record to review. Her birthplace, birth year and the year she settled in her current home are not stated; she describes herself as originally from Compton. We found no stated position or action on data centers, property taxes, development and land use, foreign or investor ownership of land or homes, police pay and pensions, or abortion clinics beyond her pro-choice statement. Her gun-policy and immigration statements come from her campaign site and from a Ballotpedia survey she completed for a U.S. House race, not for this Senate race. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey for the Senate race.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she is originally from Compton and was raised there and in Los Angeles by her aunt; Ballotpedia lists Lynwood High School and UC Santa Barbara, but her birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Twenty years as a practicing OB-GYN in Tennessee and California, a Navy medical officer (1997–2004), author and radio co-host; she has held no elected office.
qual.why: She has a long professional career but no legislative, policy, budget or local-office experience, so her work history is largely unrelated to writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: She has a long professional career but no legislative, policy, budget or local-office experience, so her work history is largely unrelated to writing law and the state budget.

second-amendment.evidence: Says she supports the Second Amendment and is a registered firearm owner, but also supports background checks and gun buyback programs as 'common sense firearm safety'.

pro-life.evidence: Says a woman has the right to choose, that medical decisions belong between patient and physician and not the government, and that every woman should have access to family planning resources.

workers-first.evidence: Says she will protect and support law-abiding immigrants. In a Ballotpedia survey for a U.S. House race she said it is time to stop ICE from removing valuable members of the community.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says teaching must be incentivized with competitive salaries, loan forgiveness and tax incentives. She states nothing on vouchers, charters or school choice.
